title: Etale sheaves on an algebraic space descend along a scheme atlas
statement: Let $B$ be a scheme and $H$ an algebraic space over $B$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], with the universes and small skeletons of [def-weil-size-convention]. Write $\operatorname{Sh}(H_{\mathrm{et}})$ for sheaves of sets [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] on the small etale scheme site, and use the inverse images and composition comparisons of [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model]. Let $p:W\to H$ be a representable surjective etale map with $W$ a scheme. Put $R=W\times_HW$ and $T=W\times_HW\times_HW$, which are schemes [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Let $p_1,p_2:R\to W$ and $p_{ij}:T\to R$ be the projections. A descent pair is a sheaf $G$ on $W_{\mathrm{et}}$ together with an isomorphism $\alpha:p_1^{-1}G\xrightarrow{\sim}p_2^{-1}G$ satisfying $p_{23}^{-1}\alpha\circ p_{12}^{-1}\alpha=p_{13}^{-1}\alpha$ under the canonical composition comparisons; a morphism of pairs is a sheaf map commuting with $\alpha$. Restriction sends a sheaf $F$ on $H_{\mathrm{et}}$ to $(p^{-1}F,\alpha_F)$, where $\alpha_F$ is the canonical identification of the two inverse images of $F$. This functor is an equivalence of categories. In particular every descent pair is effective, compatible maps glue uniquely, and an isomorphism of descent pairs glues to an isomorphism. No quasi-compactness, separation, Noetherianity or finiteness of the atlas is assumed.

source.place: Tag 05YY (lemma-descent-sheaf), statement; descent pair written using the double and triple fibre products of the scheme atlas.

proof.text: Use [lem-trf-space-enlarged-site-scheme-density] at $H$ to form the enlarged etale site $\mathcal C=\mathcal C_H$. It has terminal object $H/H$, all fibre products, and the singleton covering $\{W\to H\}$. Work on its small representative in the stipulated sheaf universe. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], the double and triple overlaps are the schemes $R$ and $T$ in the statement, and all their projection maps needed below are etale. Thus the covering and its fibre products satisfy the hypotheses of general site descent.

source.place: Tag 05YY (lemma-descent-sheaf), first proof, first paragraph; Tags 03G0 (definition-spaces-etale-site), 03G1 (lemma-compare-etale-sites).

proof.text: By [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model], for $Z=H,W,R,T$ the scheme-object restriction $E_Z:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_Z)\to\operatorname{Sh}(Z_{\mathrm{et}})$ is an equivalence, and postcomposition identifies $\mathcal C_Z$ with $\mathcal C/Z$ for these etale maps to $H$. Under these identifications inverse image is restriction, compatibly with composition. Since $H/H$ is terminal, $\mathcal C/H\cong\mathcal C$: its inverse assigns to an object its unique map to $H/H$, with the same coverings. For a sheaf $F$ on $H_{\mathrm{et}}$, extend it by $E_H$ and restrict to $W$. The two restrictions to $R$ have identical composites to $H$, so their identity comparison gives $\alpha_F$; on $T$ the three comparisons compose as identities. The cited composition comparisons identify these with exactly the inverse images and cocycle of the statement, naturally on maps.

source.place: Tag 05YY (lemma-descent-sheaf), first proof, localization and canonical identification; Tag 03LP (lemma-etale-morphism-topoi).

proof.text: Given $(G,\alpha)$, choose an extension $\widetilde G$ on $\mathcal C_W$ through $E_W$. The comparison in step 2 identifies the restrictions of $\widetilde G$ along the two projections with the extensions of $p_1^{-1}G,p_2^{-1}G$. Full faithfulness of $E_R$ therefore lifts $\alpha$ uniquely to an overlap isomorphism $\widetilde\alpha$; its inverse lifts the inverse of $\alpha$. Faithfulness of $E_T$ shows that its triple-overlap cocycle holds, since the two composites restrict to the asserted cocycle for $\alpha$. These are precisely gluing data for the singleton covering of step 1. Here the repeated cover index still has overlap $W\times_HW$, not just $W$; no extra diagonal axiom is needed. Indeed pulling the cocycle to $(w,w,w)$ gives $d^*\alpha\circ d^*\alpha=d^*\alpha$, hence $d^*\alpha=1$ by cancellation.

source.place: Tag 05YY (lemma-descent-sheaf), first proof: the diagram is the cocycle condition for gluing data; sites.tex gluing data before Tag 04TR (lemma-glue-sheaves).

proof.text: Apply [lem-pe-set-sheaf-cover-descent] to $\mathcal C$, $U=H$, the singleton index set, and $(\widetilde G,\widetilde\alpha)$. The site is small with all fibre products by step 1, and the chosen universe contains the index set and products. It gives a sheaf $\widetilde F$ on $\mathcal C/H$ and an isomorphism $\widetilde F|_W\simeq\widetilde G$ intertwining the overlap data. Identify $\mathcal C/H$ with $\mathcal C$ as in step 2 and put $F=E_H\widetilde F$. Under the equivalences of step 2 this gives an isomorphism from the restriction pair of $F$ to $(G,\alpha)$. Every descent pair is therefore effective.

source.place: Tag 05YY (lemma-descent-sheaf), first proof, final sentence, invoking Sites gluing; sites.tex Tag 04TR (lemma-glue-sheaves).

proof.text: Let $F_1,F_2$ be sheaves on $H_{\mathrm{et}}$. Extend them to $\mathcal C$. A map between their descent pairs lifts uniquely on $\mathcal C/W$ by full faithfulness of $E_W$; its compatibility with $\alpha$ says precisely that its two restrictions agree on $\mathcal C/R$, by faithfulness of $E_R$ and step 2. The morphism clause of [lem-pe-set-sheaf-cover-descent] glues it uniquely on $\mathcal C/H$. Thus restriction is fully faithful. Choose the realizations of step 4 for objects and use this unique gluing for arrows: uniqueness gives preservation of identity and composition and gives the inverse natural comparisons. This constructs an equivalence. If the local map is an isomorphism, its inverse also commutes with the overlap data; glue both maps, and uniqueness identifies their composites with identities. Hence an isomorphism of pairs glues to an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 05YY (lemma-descent-sheaf), first proof; sites.tex Tag 04TQ (lemma-glue-maps) and Tag 04TS (lemma-mapping-property-glue).
